items.title: Aesthetic-Usability Effect
items.origin: Kurosu e Kashimura, 1995, avaliação de interfaces ATM
items.definition: A aparência pode melhorar usabilidade percebida sem melhorar desempenho real.
items.application: Melhorar legibilidade e hierarquia das questões.
items.limits: Não aceitar estética como prova de usabilidade.
items.acceptance: Comparar satisfação, sucesso, erros e tempo.

items.limits: Não inventar progresso, atrasar artificialmente ou confundir feedback com confirmação.

additional_evidence.finding: Mean effect was near zero across 63 conditions; considerable variability. Do not infer overload from option count alone.
Complexity, decision difficulty, preference uncertainty and decision goals moderate choice overload.
Around 3–5 separate items under particular experimental conditions; no universal UI item cap.
Recall advantage of unfinished tasks is not universal; distinguish the tendency to resume interrupted tasks (Ovsiankina effect). Support safe resumption rather than memory or engagement promises.
Overly broad tolerance can harm maintainability and long-term interoperability; explicit protocols and active maintenance are preferred.
